- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3–5 day moving average before forecasting to reduce noise.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7), model often fails to capture mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early periods when sentiment is bullish; apply downward bias of 2–5% for first 7–10 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 2+ consecutive high then low), model often misses the turn; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
